Architectural Review Board tables solar panel plan for 633 Mildrid Avenue
Board members raised concerns that an AI-generated rendering made the panel layout appear distorted and asked the installer to consult the homeowner about a symmetrical redesign.
The Architectural Review Board voted to table a vote on a solar panel installation at 633 Mildrid Avenue, asking the installer to check with the homeowner about rearranging panels for symmetry before resubmitting.
The meeting took place Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026. Michael Nhouse, with Berto Electric, presented the project, which included 10 new panels alongside two existing rectangular arrays.
THE SYMMETRY CONCERN Board member Tracy raised the first objection to the layout shown in the rendering. "I think it looks fine on the dormer because it kind of goes away, but this feels so prominent on the front of the house," Tracy said, adding, "And the fact that it's not symmetrical, you know, there's not panels on both sides."
Another board member questioned whether the rendering was accurate, noting the dormer appeared off-center. Nhouse acknowledged the image was AI-generated and said the true prints would show a difference of "probably about a foot off" from what was depicted.
A PROPOSED FIX Board member Bob suggested relocating two panels to the opposite side of the dormer and adding a third panel there instead, arguing it would preserve production while achieving symmetry. "If we did that, we could add an additional panel and that could offset the difference," a board member said.
A board member said, "I think if it was if you could do that and be successful, I think it would be more successful aesthetically." Board member David said, "I'm okay with how it is right now. But, but I do I do agree that it would be an improvement visually if you did it that way."
Nhouse said the homeowner did not want panels moved to that side due to reduced sun exposure, but agreed to raise the board's suggestion with the homeowner.
WHAT HAPPENS NEXT The board agreed to table the vote so Nhouse could consult the homeowner. If the homeowner agrees to a symmetrical layout, the revised plan could be approved administratively without returning to the board; if not, the project will come back for another hearing.
